title: Case D — high-rise among city blocks
summary: 1:1:4 tower in a regular array of 82 low blocks, pedestrian-height scalar speed (thermistor, 3 wind directions) plus a 33-point split-fibre velocity field at WD = 0.

configuration.blocks: 82 blocks of 0.4H x 0.4H x 0.1H = 100 x 100 x 25 mm
configuration.roads: 0.1H / 0.2H / 0.3H = 25 / 50 / 75 mm; 9 columns in x (pitch alternating 175 / 150 mm), 11 rows in y (pitch 125 mm); corners cut by the turntable circle
configuration.scale: 1:400 (H = 100 m full scale; the 5 mm measurement plane = 2 m)
configuration.instrument: thermistor anemometer (78 points x 3 directions; 66 measured per direction, 12 points in the band around the tower unmeasured) and split-fibre probe (33 points at WD = 0: U, V, W, variances, k)
configuration.tunnel: see the data paper (Kikumoto et al. 2026, section 3.4)

units.length: m (model scale; converted from the workbook's millimetres)

frame.origin: tower centre on the ground plane (the array's bounding box is centred on it)
frame.x: +x streamwise at WD = 0 (the 0 deg thermistor field is exactly y-mirror symmetric; the split-fibre U is positive at the stream-like points and negative in the tower's windward horseshoe)
frame.wind_direction_rotation: +x toward +y, read from Figure 4 of the data paper. The array is exactly y-mirror symmetric, so the rotation sense CANNOT be settled from the measurements: headings +theta and -theta give exact mirror fields. Treat 22.5 and 45 deg with that caveat.

inflow_fit.method: log law, kappa = 0.41, least squares on the workbook's 13-point profile (z = 5 ... 1200 mm); two windows, because the measurement plane z/H = 0.02 sits below the 0.02 ... 2H window used for Cases A and B
inflow_fit.note: derived during scoping, not published by AIJ; a log-law inlet cannot be right at both the measurement plane and the upper profile

gotchas: All of Case D's data lives in LF_caseD.xls, a genuine OLE2/BIFF8 workbook (read it with xlrd 2.x; openpyxl cannot). Sheets: 'Geometry&Points', 'Inflow', 'Results (Exp_S)' (split fibre, WD = 0), 'Results (Exp_T)' (thermistor, 0 / 22.5 / 45 deg).
Coordinates are millimetres in the workbook; the API serves metres.

The shipped BD_caseD.stl is dirty: 1572 facets of which 576 are duplicates, and all 83 roofs are wound inward (signed volume 0.011159 m^3 against the true 0.021477 m^3). The API's geometry.stl is rebuilt from the 83 shells' bounding boxes: 996 facets, watertight, volume 0.021477 m^3.

The thermistor reads a SCALAR speed. Over the 33 points where both instruments overlap at WD = 0, the ratio of mean thermistor speed to mean |U| is 1.342 (the mean of the per-point ratios is 1.50). sqrt(|U|^2 + 2k) from the split-fibre data matches the thermistor to FB +0.058, R 0.947; |U| alone to FB +0.292, R 0.872.
Unmeasured thermistor cells are '-' in the workbook (null here). At WD = 0 the 66 measured values are 33 exact mirror pairs, so only 33 are independent; at 22.5 and 45 deg all 66 are independent.
A prior Eddy3D comparison kept in the folder (case-d-eddy3d-prior-comparison.xlsx) scores R = +0.096 against the thermistor: a frame or geometry error, not a closure result. It is not a validation.
doi_note: The case folder ships without the Zenodo record's readme and CSVs; they are mirrored byte for byte under clean/sources/zenodo_caseD/ (people and DOI from that readme and the data paper's reference 50).
citation_requested: Kikumoto, H. et al. (2026). Japan Architectural Review 9(1), e70083, section 3.4.
